sources.quote: Evergy also offers one time-based rate plan to its Kansas customers, but is not switching them to this plan automatically.
sources.searcher_note: Same page, two paragraphs earlier: 'More than 99% of the company's Missouri customers are now on a time-based plan', per an Evergy spokesperson. Covers Missouri Metro + West together, Dec 2023; lead has Evergy Metro Missouri at 89.7% for 2024 (EIA filing). Kansas: opt-in only, no Kansas count given.

sources.quote: all 550,000 Evergy residential customers in the state will be moved to an aggressive time-of-use rate this fall
sources.searcher_note: Earliest found. Missouri PSC-ordered switch of all Evergy Missouri residential customers to time-of-use in fall 2023; contrasts Ameren Missouri's more gradual rollout. Forward-looking, no enrollment percentages.

sources.quote: The commission, which regulates Missouri utilities, ordered Evergy to implement time-of-use pricing, which places a premium on electricity used during periods of high demand.
sources.searcher_note: Missouri PSC approved a milder default time-of-use plan for Evergy Missouri customers who did not pick a plan. No Kansas mention, no enrollment counts.

sources.quote: The Missouri Public Service Commission has entered orders and approved tariffs to transition almost all residential electric customers of regulated utilities
sources.searcher_note: Sentence continues 'to Time-Based rates'. Names all four Missouri investor-owned utilities (Evergy Missouri West, Evergy Missouri Metro, Ameren Missouri, Liberty) and says Ameren and Liberty transitions run on their own timelines. Supports the lead's all-four-Missouri-IOUs claim in words; no percentages.

sources.quote: standard opt-in enrollments in time-based plans see about one-percent conversion.
sources.searcher_note: Case study of Evergy's Missouri time-of-use transition: about 30 percent (roughly 160,000) of residential Missouri customers pre-enrolled before automatic conversion to the Default Time Based Plan; contrasts with ~1% for opt-in programs (the Kansas-style setup). Date from upload path only.

notes: The Missouri-mandatory vs Kansas-opt-in split for Evergy is widely reported (KC Star, KCUR, E&E News, Missouri Independent, Fox4). No source found states the Kansas share (1.6%, 3,904 homes) or the Evergy Metro Missouri figure (89.7%, 245,547 homes) or runs the 2019-2024 EIA comparison. The only Missouri percentage found is the KC Star's 'more than 99%' of Evergy's Missouri customers on a time-based plan as of Dec 2023 (spokesperson figure, Metro + West combined); the lead's 89.7% is Evergy Metro only, for 2024, from EIA-861. One logged query (the 2026 opt-out one) was expanded by the search tool into several follow-up searches on its own; none found 2026 enrollment figures.
